messages.subject: Minimum Spanning Networks
parts:
Hi,
 I want to draw MSNs without showing name of isolates or name of MLGs on each circle. When I type "Null" in the command, MLGs or the name of isolates are not shown, but some little numbers will be added by the software showing the number of isolates in each MLG. I don't know how I can get rid of those little numbers on each circle.

Also, I have four populations and I want to show MNSs for all of them and then I want to show the relationships between each of two populations in different figures. My problem is that when I use a palette to show different colors for all clusters in a MSN  (for example "funky" palette) and  I use the same palette to draw a MSN for two populations, the program changes the color of these two populations (for example population 1 is green, 2 is blue , 3 is red and 4 is yellow in MSNs for all four populations. When I want to draw  a MSN for just populations 1 and 2, the program changes the color of pop 1 and 2 for example they will be brown and red instead of green and blue).  how I can use the same color for two populations as what we see in MSNs for all populations.
          Also the color of populations are so close to each other , Is there any way that we can use ColorBrewer palettes for MSNs?

Thank you,

Vahideh

messages.author: d192ec4b1d416345
messages.subject: Re: [poppr] Minimum Spanning Networks
parts:
Hi Vahideh,

All the solutions you are seeking are in the documentation for plot_poppr_msn (type ?plot_poppr_msn in your R console): https://www.rdocumentation.org/packages/poppr/versions/2.2.1/topics/plot_poppr_msn

For the numbers in the circles, you can set nodelab = 1e6 in the function call. 

Regarding colors, you don't have to use a palette function. You can use a vector of named colors. From the examples in the documentation:

data(partial_clone)
pcmsn <- bruvo.msn(partial_clone, replen = rep(1, 10))

# You can plot using a color palette or a vector of named colors
# Here's a way to define the colors beforehand
pc_colors <- nPop(partial_clone) %>%
  RColorBrewer::brewer.pal("Set2") %>%
  setNames(popNames(partial_clone))

pc_colors

# Labelling the samples contained in multilocus genotype 9
set.seed(999)
plot_poppr_msn(partial_clone, pcmsn, palette = pc_colors, inds = 9)



Hope that helps!
Zhian
